title: Hook propagation experiments scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
- Personal scratchpad for the tracehook/ingest instability saga. Trying to capture commands, snippets, short experiments, and quick hypotheses so we don't lose tribal knowledge during on-call.

Symptoms observed (summary):
- Intermittent drop in trace count (~40-70% reduction) starting around 2025-11-02 22:10 UTC.
- Prometheus metric tracehook.spans.received dropped from ~22k/min to 7–12k/min for some customers; other tenants unaffected.
- Kafka consumer lag on ingestion topic spiked briefly (consumer-group obs-ingest-hook) then recovered.
- Correlated occasional 502s from tracehook sidecar in front of ingest API and repeated TLS handshake logs during peaks.

Quick timeline (rough):
- 2025-11-02 21:50 UTC: First customer alert (reduced traces).
- 2025-11-02 22:05 UTC: Pager duty triggered.
- 2025-11-02 22:12 UTC: I restarted obs-tracehook deployment on cluster-3 (hotfix #1). Partial recovery observed for ~8m.
- 2025-11-03 02:30 UTC: Canary rollout of obs-ingest v1.12.3 (included sidecar config change) — correlated second drop.

Commands I ran (useful for repro / notes):
- kubectl logs -n observability deploy/obs-tracehook -c tracehook --since=2h | grep -i "error" | tail -n 200
- kubectl exec -n observability -it obs-tracehook-pod -- curl -sv https://127.0.0.1:8443/healthz 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
- kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-1:9092 --describe --group obs-ingest-hook | tee /tmp/consumer-lag-20251103.txt
- tcpdump -nni any port 9092 and host 10.23.45.67 -w /tmp/kafka-tcpdump.pcap (ran for 60s during spike)
- kubectl get events -n observability --field-selector involvedObject.name=obs-tracehook -o wide | tail -n 50
- curl -v -X POST "https://ingest.internal/v1/traces" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @small-batch.json -i

Observed error snippets (copied verbatim):
- "2025-11-02T22:11:53Z ERROR [ingest] tls: handshake failure from 10.2.14.8:45212"
- "WARN  ingest.kafka.consumer - requeueing batch, kafka broker error: Broker: Unknown server error (code 500)"
- "ERROR tracehook.backpressure - write timeout after 10s to kafka producer"
- "prometheus: scrape failed for tracehook: read tcp 10.23.45.12:443->... i/o timeout"

Quick grep of logs around TLS errors:
- kubectl logs -n observability deploy/obs-tracehook -c sidecar --since=30m | grep -i "handshake" | head -n 20
  -> entries show client IPs from both cloud-1 and cloud-2; some show SNI mismatch: "tls: client requested server name "ingest" but server is configured for "tracehook.local""

Hypotheses (ranked, quick):
1) Sidecar/ingest config drift: the canary rollout changed sidecar TLS/SNI behavior (changed envoy filter) causing handshake mismatches for some tenants. Explains partial recovery after restart (new pods temporarily have older config).
2) Intermittent Kafka broker 500 errors causing backpressure; hook process enters slow-path and drops sampling. Evidence: broker 500 logs and producer write timeouts.
3) Sampling config bug in tracehook where per-tenant sampling table corrupted during config reload; manifests as tiered drops.
4) Network path MTU or proxy cutting chunks (less likely but saw occasional "unexpected EOF" on large batches).

Experiments tried (and results):
- Rollback attempt: redeployed obs-ingest to previous image v1.12.2 on cluster-3 at 2025-11-03 03:10 UTC -> immediate partial recovery for affected tenants; suggests ingest-side change was involved.
- Sidecar toggle: set TRACEHOOK_SIDECAR_TLS_STRICT=false in a single pod via kubectl set env -> pod restarted -> that pod accepted connections w/o handshake errors for 30m.
- Reduced batch_size to 8 for a noisy tenant (env OVERRIDE_BATCH_SIZE=8) -> producer write timeout frequency reduced but total throughput still lower than baseline.

Data pulled for investigation (files/notes):
- /tmp/consumer-lag-20251103.txt (kafka group describe output)
- /tmp/kafka-tcpdump.pcap (tcpdump capture during spike)
- prod-tracehook-2h-logs-20251102.gz (archived logs pulled via s3 cp)

Actionable short-term remediation (what we did):
- Rolled back obs-ingest canary in cluster-3.
- Increased ingress retry window (kafka producer retries -> 5).
- Enabled verbose sidecar TLS logs for next 24h.

Longer-term follow-ups (next steps / backlog):
- Reproduce handshake mismatch in staging with the same envoy filter + mTLS cert rotation. Create small harness that emulates multi-tenant SNI behavior. (owner: Priya)
- Add per-tenant ingest success/failure counters exposed to Prometheus so we can quickly identify tenant-specific drops (owner: Maya).
- Audit rollout playbook to ensure sidecar filter changes are gated by a canary tenant set and smoke tests hitting all SNI names (owner: Tom).
- Run a focused Kafka broker health check and broker-side logs review around timestamps of 2025-11-02T22:00-23:00 UTC (owner: infra-kafka team).

Notes for on-call handoff:
- If trace counts drop again: check tracehook sidecar TLS handshake logs first (kubectl logs -c sidecar).
- Check kafka consumer-group lag and broker 5xxs: kafka-consumer-groups.sh + look at broker logs in prod-kafka-cluster-1/2.
- Quick mitigation: scale tracehook replicas + toggle non-strict TLS env to see if TLS mismatches are root cause. Use caution: non-strict TLS is temporary and only for debugging.

Open questions / unknowns: 
- Why did restart produce a short-lived recovery then relapse? (config drift vs transient broker errors?)
- Are there tenants for whom data is being silently dropped before producing into Kafka (sampling code path) — need to add counters.
- Did the canary rollout progressively flip a config flag between control-plane and sidecars? Need to audit CI deploy job for envoy-filter templating.

Small checklist to complete before we close this incident:
- [ ] Confirm rollback is stable for 48h on all clusters where canary ran.
- [ ] Deploy per-tenant success metrics to staging and validate alert rules.
- [ ] Reproduce handshake mismatch in staging and fix envoy filter template.
- [ ] Post-mortem draft (include timeline, root cause, mitigations) and link to OBS-4523.

References and quick links:
- OBS ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-4523
- PR that introduced sidecar change: https://github.com/redwood/obs/pull/987
- Tracehook runbook (internal): confluence:Obs Tracehook Runbook

Misc notes (random thoughts I scribbled while pacing):
- Could caching of TLS certs at LB cause stale SNI routing? If LB caches SNI -> wrong cert returned -> handshake fails. Worth checking LB config.
- If Kafka 500s are the trigger, we need better backlog alerting (peak retry-rate metric).
- Consider circuit-breaker on tracehook producer so individual tenant spikes don't push the whole system into slow-path.

-- end of scratchpad --
